transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-03-02 10:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ben Kline (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Novus CTO), Marco Ruiz (Lead ML Eng), Liza Chen (Head of Security)

Summary:
Novus Labs is evaluating options to move away from a mixed OpenAI + vLLM self-hosted stack toward a more predictable inference platform. They are interested in Hosted for quick wins, but have strict compliance (data residency, KMS) and performance needs that may push them toward Dedicated or Private. Key asks: eval parity with current outputs, latency/cost tradeoffs, private VPC deployment details, KMS/HSM integration, and a baseline benchmarking plan.

Topics discussed:
- Current stack and pain points (OpenAI + vLLM for tail workloads)
- Compatibility with vLLM/TGI model formats and weights
- Eval parity and result drift concerns
- Hosting options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC
- Operational controls: canary rollouts, KV cache, batching, and autoscaling
- Next steps: benchmarks, security docs, pilot pricing

Action items called out in the call (captured conversationally):
- Ben will sketch a benchmark config and provide a small infra snippet for a dedicated test cluster.
- Sofia to send security/compliance pack and pilot pricing estimate.
- Priya to assemble representative prompts and usage patterns.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I think we have about 55 minutes, right? Quick intros?
[00:06] Priya Desai: Yep, Priya here, CTO at Novus. Marco and Liza are with me. We're mainly trying to figure out if we can consolidate our inference footprint.
[00:12] Marco Ruiz: Hi, Marco, lead on the ML infra side. We're running some stuff on OpenAI for chat endpoints and self-host vLLM for batch and low-cost inference.
[00:20] Liza Chen: Liza, head of security, I'll focus on compliance and data flow questions.
[00:24] Ben Kline: Ben from Redwood, SE, happy to dig into compatibility and performance.
[00:28] Sofia Martinez: Great. Priya, can you give a quick snapshot of your stack and the trigger for this evaluation?
[00:34] Priya Desai: Sure. So today... we have a mixed approach. OpenAI for our real-time conversational endpoints because of the managed tooling like function-calling and streaming. For higher volume inference and cost optimization we run vLLM on prem-ish — it's on EC2 instances in our VPC. The problem is the maintenance and drift, and we want predictability on latency and cost. We're also seeing limits from OpenAI on throughput sometimes.
[00:56] Marco Ruiz: Also some models behave differently on OpenAI versus our locally quantized vLLM versions — so eval parity is a real worry. We saw differences on safety and hallucination rates after quantization.
[01:10] Ben Kline: Yeah that's common. Two angles we usually take: model parity testing during onboarding, and runtime knobs — quantization profiles, KV cache, and batching configs — to tune cost vs latency. We can run a Repro eval suite to show diff across variants.
[01:28] Liza Chen: Important for us: KMS integration, where keys stay in our cloud KMS; audit logs for every inference; and network isolation — so if Redwood's hosted path can't meet that, we need Private.
[01:40] Sofia Martinez: Makes sense. We offer Hosted for the fastest start, Dedicated (reserved capacity) for predictable throughput with tenant isolation, and Private for a VPC/private plane or on-prem. For KMS: Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations; Dedicated sometimes supports bring-your-key depending on contract.
[02:00] Priya Desai: When you say Dedicated, is that single-tenant hardware in a cloud region or is it multi-tenant with isolation?
[02:06] Ben Kline: Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool dedicated to you — compute's not multi-tenant. The control plane still has some managed components unless you pick Private which gives you a private control plane option.
[02:18] Marco Ruiz: We need to be able to pin model versions. We had an incident where auto-update broke prompt output. How does Redwood handle rollouts and model pinning?
[02:28] Ben Kline: You can pin model versions per route. We support canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback to compatible variants. We'll keep previous versions available for rollback.
[02:36] Priya Desai: Good. Another concern: can we run our current vLLM/TGI artifacts as-is? We heavily use some custom kernels and custom tokenizer tweaks.
[02:46] Ben Kline: We try to be flexible. For vLLM/TGI artifacts, we typically accept standard model weights/checkpoints. Custom kernels can be trickier — we may need to recompile or map kernels to our runtime. We can do a small compatibility spike. If you have a sample Docker or the model repo, Ben: we'll attempt a port.
[03:05] Marco Ruiz: We do have a repo. It uses some patched vLLM and a TGI wrapper for streaming. We can share a minimal example.
[03:12] Liza Chen: Also, data residency — some PII routes must stay in EU. Do you offer region pinning for Hosted?
[03:20] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we have cloud regions in EU and NA. Hosted can be region-pinned, Dedicated obviously sits in the region you select, Private gives full control on-prem or VPC.
[03:30] Priya Desai: Latency targets are tight for interactive products — p95 under 250ms for short prompts. Can you hit that?
[03:38] Ben Kline: Depends on model size and token counts. For small-to-medium models on Dedicated in the same region we see p95 under 200ms for short sequences with continuous batching tuned properly. We'll need to know token lengths and concurrency.
[03:52] Marco Ruiz: Our heavy flows are about 128 tokens average with bursts to 512 for summarization. Concurrency around 80 concurrent connections during peak.
[04:02] Ben Kline: That's helpful. We'll size a benchmark cluster for that and suggest batching/auto-scale policies. We'll include latency and cost per token estimates.
[04:12] Sofia Martinez: On the topic of eval parity — Marco you mentioned hallucination delta after quant — we can do a side-by-side on your prompts: OpenAI baseline, your vLLM quantized, and Redwood-hosted variant. We run the same seed and temperature settings as far as possible.
[04:26] Marco Ruiz: How reproducible is the output? Tokenization differences exist between TGI wrappers and other runtimes.
[04:32] Ben Kline: We surface tokenization maps and will instrument the eval harness to normalize tokenizers. There will always be tiny differences but typically we can get within an acceptable tolerance.
[04:44] Liza Chen: Security question — how are audit logs exposed? We need immutable logs for 365 days and integration with our SIEM.
[04:52] Sofia Martinez: For Dedicated and Private, we can stream audit logs to your S3 or your SIEM with signed envelopes. Hosted also supports audit export for enterprise customers. We'll include retention options in the security pack.
[05:06] Priya Desai: For KMS, we want to manage keys and prevent Redwood from decrypting content in transit. Does Redwood support envelope encryption with customer keys?
[05:14] Ben Kline: Yes, Private supports BYOK with envelope encryption patterns against your KMS, and Dedicated can be configured in many enterprise agreements. We'll detail that in the security doc.
[05:26] Marco Ruiz: Ok ops question — what's the deployment model if we pick Private? Full air-gapped on-prem or VPC with a private control plane?
[05:34] Sofia Martinez: Both. We offer a private control plane that lives in your VPC with a customer-managed ingress, or a fully on-prem package for regulated environments. The on-prem path is heavier effort but supported.
[05:44] Priya Desai: Cost question — rough ballpark for a pilot for our workload?
[05:49] Sofia Martinez: We can do a 4-week pilot— rough estimate depends on the chosen plan. For Dedicated pilot with a small GPU pool and support, expect a starting commitment — we'll give a ballpark in writing. We'll include price per token comparisons versus your current spend.
[06:03] Marco Ruiz: Who's the contact for the technical setup?
[06:06] Ben Kline: I'll own the tech spike and benchmarking with you. Sofia will handle contracting and pricing.
[06:11] Priya Desai: Great. Can you also show us how function-calling and streaming map to your runtime? Our chat depends on function-calling for structured outputs to downstream services.
[06:20] Ben Kline: Yes, we support streaming and function calling. If you have existing function schemas, we can wire those into Redwood endpoints and show example responses.
[06:29] Liza Chen: A final compliance nit: do you have SOC2 Type II? And any ISO27001?
[06:34] Sofia Martinez: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001; we'll include the certificates and the SOC2 report redacted in the security pack.
[06:43] Priya Desai: Ok, so next steps from our side: we'll pull together representative prompts and the model repo snippet. From Redwood: benchmarks and security pack. Timeline?
[06:54] Ben Kline: If you can share prompts and a minimal vLLM/TGI sample by end of week, we can spin up a benchmark cluster next week and aim to share initial results in 7–10 business days.
[07:06] Sofia Martinez: I'll send the SOW template and a pilot pricing ballpark by Friday.
[07:10] Priya Desai: Sounds good. Any potential blockers?
[07:14] Ben Kline: The main risk is custom kernel compatibility. If your vLLM has deep patches, we may need small porting work. We'll call that out in the spike and estimate time.
[07:26] Marco Ruiz: Noted. Also want to validate streaming parity — sometimes streaming chunk boundaries differ and downstream parsers choke.
[07:31] Ben Kline: We'll include streaming chunk tests in the benchmark harness.
[07:36] Sofia Martinez: Anything else?
[07:38] Liza Chen: We might ask for a data flow diagram once we see the security pack.
[07:42] Sofia Martinez: Will do.
[07:45] Priya Desai: That's it from me. Thanks all.
[07:48] Sofia Martinez: Great, recap of next steps: Redwood to send security pack and pricing; Ben to run compatibility spike and benchmark harness once prompts and model sample are provided; Novus to provide prompt sets and repo access. We'll target follow-ups in the next two weeks.
[07:59] Ben Kline: I'll follow up with a benchmark plan doc and a short Terraform snippet for the dedicated test cluster.
[08:06] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone, we'll send notes and actions.
